note: Source anchors in `tolerated` name SYMBOLS, not line numbers (since 9.86.1 — the 9.86.0 rows cited buildToolRegistry.ts lines from the 9.85.0 tree that the same release had moved by ~29 lines). Recorded state of every offer/dispatch divergence the walk in test/core/agent/toolDivergenceWalk.test.ts can reach. This is a RATCHET, not a gate: a divergence that is not here FAILS (it is new), one that is here and stops appearing FAILS (behaviour moved), and one that changes shape FAILS. `tolerated` is hand-written and required — a row whose reason is empty, reads todo/tbd/fixme/xxx in any case, or is shorter than 40 characters FAILS, so accepting debt is a person's sentence in a diff somebody reviewed rather than a side effect of running the re-record. A row that says a defect is real rather than intended names its entry in docs/design/2026-09-recorded-not-built.md, which carries what fixing it would cost. Re-record with AF_DIVERGENCE_BASELINE=update npx vitest run test/core/agent/toolDivergenceWalk.test.ts, then write the reason for every new row.

framework/read_skill-vs-static.because: Agent: tool name 'read_skill' is reserved when ≥1 Skill is registered. Rename your custom 'read_skill' tool or unregister it.

framework/skip_step-vs-static.because: Agent: tool name 'skip_step' is reserved when any skill declares `steps` — the framework auto-attaches the procedure-integrity tool under that name, and a same-named tool would silently take over the model's recorded skips. Rename your tool.

framework/run_overview-vs-static.because: AgentBuilder.selfExplain: tool name 'run_overview' is reserved by .selfExplain() (inline mode). The tools slot dedupes by name (first wins), so your tool would silently shadow the trace tool. Rename it, or reserved names: run_overview, find_context_errors, find_in_trace, trace_node, trace_slice, backtrack, who_wrote, get_value, inspect_tool_call, inspect_tool_run, read_narrative.

framework/present-vs-static.because: Agent: tool name 'present' is reserved when an artifact store is attached — the framework auto-attaches the hand-to-the-screen tool under that name, and a same-named tool would silently take over the model's presentations. collision/mcp-then-skill-active::shared_.configuration: 'shared_tool' claimed by an MCP-served tool, mounted through a provider AND an ACTIVE scoped skill’s `tools:[]` (`.toolsFromActiveSkill()`, activated)
collision/mcp-then-skill-active::shared_.cause: 'skill-active' registered 'shared_tool' and neither its schema nor its implementation was ever reachable; reported as a dead claim by tools.claim_swallowed, once per epoch it lost
collision/mcp-then-skill-active::shared_.tolerated: A scoped skill's tool (activated; its contract competed and lost) under a name a ToolProvider serves. The provider merges ahead of the skill's injection, so the provider's contract is the wire's — and since 9.92.0 dispatch follows the offer, so the provider's implementation answers; the skill's tool loses the wire AND the dispatch while the provider holds the name. Until 9.92.0 this configuration was a contract-swap (the skill's execute answered the provider's contract); the swap is closed and the dead claim is reported by agentfootprint.tools.claim_swallowed once per epoch. Tolerated because a provider's list is a per-iteration fact and the merge order (provider before injection) is the documented law; a rename is the fix and the event names both parties.

collision/mcp-then-skill-inactive::share.configuration: 'shared_tool' claimed by an MCP-served tool, mounted through a provider AND an INACTIVE scoped skill’s `tools:[]` (`.toolsFromActiveSkill()`, never activated)

collision/mcp-then-skill-static::shared_.configuration: 'shared_tool' claimed by an MCP-served tool, mounted through a provider AND a skill’s `tools:[]` with tools always visible (no `autoActivate`)
collision/mcp-then-skill-static::shared_.cause: 'mcp' registered 'shared_tool' and neither its schema nor its implementation was ever reachable; reported as a dead claim by tools.claim_swallowed, once per epoch it lost
collision/mcp-then-skill-static::shared_.tolerated: The mirror of the shadow seam, unreported until 9.92.0. The merge is first-occurrence-wins with the static registry list first, and lookupTool reads registryByName before the provider cache — so a provider tool whose name a registry-list holder already owns loses the wire AND dispatch, and is dead in both directions. reportShadowedTools could not see it before 9.92.0: it fired only when a provider schema SURVIVED the merge. The model is never misled here (it reads one contract and calls that same implementation), so this is the author's problem rather than the model's — but it is silent, and the build cannot refuse it because the provider's list is per-iteration. Reporting it is a behaviour change. Since 9.92.0 the claim is REPORTED, not silent: agentfootprint.tools.claim_swallowed names the loser and the winner on every epoch the name was held (the `reported` column carries it), so the row records a dead claim the operator is told about. Still a divergence because the tool exists and nothing can reach it; still tolerated because refusing it needs a build-time moment a per-iteration provider list does not have, and silently hoisting the loser onto the wire would take a name away from the party that holds it today.
